title: Banishment
text: “I wonder what these fellows are competing over,” I said.
“Stop screwing around and change me back!” Ren was making a fuss, completely oblivious to the mood. What a noisy fellow, I say.
“What a tiresome man, devoid of any sentiment. Well, it can’t be helped, nano. Four Fairy Morph, nano.”
I cast Fairy Morph and turned Ren back. Poof! And just like that, Ren was stark naked.
“Alright! …wait, GYAAAAAAAAAH!?”
The naked Ren came to his senses and let out a scream. Why was he making such a fuss over something so obvious?
“Don’t just change me back out of nowhere!”
“Boo…”
Oh? Luna was voicing her protest over there. Keel had been away with Big Sister and the others this time. Kuro-chan, on the other hand, seemed to be enjoying the turn of events.
“Ohh, the Black Swordsman revives—Great Release! The demon blade is drawn? The Black Swordsman’s demon blade awakens, thirsting for blood tonight—”
“Kuro-chan, given the situation, that’s less middle-school edgelord talk and more of a euphemism, isn’t it? ‘The demon blade drawn’… ‘thirsting for blood’…”
“A love-drawing technique with Keel-kun—”
“Luna-chan, please stop pushing the Ren-and-Keel-kun relationship forward.”
“Well, it can’t be helped, nano. Fairy Morph, nano.”
I turned him into an inult again.
“Hey! Quit messing around! Turn me back into a human!”
“Which is it going to be!? This is such a hassle, I say.”
“Ugh, this is getting confusing…”
Anyway, the noisy, demanding Ren finally secured some clothes before returning to human form.
“Finally, I’m free of that pathetic shape.”
“If Luna-chan ever requests it, I’ll turn you into an inult again, indeed.”
Back in the loop when I’d learned Fairy Morph, I’d turned Ren into an inult quite often.
“Do that and I’ll kill you!”
Ren lunged at me, radiating bloodlust as if seizing the perfect opportunity, but I swiftly dodged and countered with a Paralyze Lance straight through him.
“Gah—”
“Boo.”
Kuro-chan voiced her protest at Ren’s undignified state, I say.
“Honestly, Ren-san, you really do expose yourself in such pathetic ways too often,” said Itsuki.
“D-damn it… says the guy who’s letting Motoyasu off the hook?”
“I never said that, did I? I just can’t beat Motoyasu-san right now, so I’ll sharpen my fangs before taking revenge. Other than that, all I can do is harass him outside of combat.”
Pitter-patter, Itsuki scurried into Father’s arms and started rubbing against him.
“What are you doing!? That’s my spot, I say!”
“Naofumi-san, this is the best way to punish Motoyasu-san. Come on, let’s have you pet me and Wolf as much as possible.”
“Itsuki… so this is the method you choose just because you can’t win otherwise, huh.”
“Woof-peon!”
“Wolf’s jumping on the bandwagon too… you two are pretty shrewd, huh.”
Father, at Itsuki’s request, was petting them. Grrrr, I say!
“Look, even you, Rabbit Guy, get an advantage over usaunnies with that size of yours, so you should cling to Naofumi-san too.”
“And if I do that, don’t I incur a massive disadvantage? Being resented by that man never leads to anything good, so I’d rather not get involved.”
“Well, using this kind of underhanded approach against Spear Hero is a good move, nano. It really is more effective than a direct assault, nano.”
Bow Hero, twisted as he is, isn’t wrong about his methods, nano—so Rival spouted off. After that, Rival wrote out the Four Fairy Morph spell formula in a notebook and taught it to Ren and Itsuki.
“With this, I can finally turn back into a human whenever I want! Thanks to Gaelion, I’ve learned magic too—everything’s coming up roses.”
“Fu… Four Fairy Morph.”
Poof, Rafumi turned Ren into an inult.
“Gwaaaaah!? Rafumi!!”
“So you can use it after all!”
“I merely happen to know the formula, is all. Without a proper Hero’s weapon, I can’t use it very well, you know.”
“I’ll definitely make you pay for this someday!”

Ren was fuming with rage. Well, whatever the case, this solved the problem of Rival thinking she’d gained some sort of advantage over me! But Father had taken to giving me lectures about needing to reflect, and had started leaving me out of conversations more often. How strange, I say. I hadn’t done anything wrong at all!

The day after all that commotion, I say. At Melromarc Castle, King Azott and Ren’s companions—who had been keeping watch over developments at the castle—came to report that the tiger siblings, my Fiancée, and even Filo-tan had suddenly vanished. Apparently, around the time we were having our great brawl, a massive explosion had occurred near Trash’s chambers in Melromarc. When Rafumi and the others rushed to the scene… Trash was there, and it seems they ended up having a conversation in the throne room.

“This time, I have summoned Sir Amaki, the Sword Hero, for no other reason than this: the Melty you brought back has been the victim of an incident caused by those beastmen of Siltvelt and the Shield Devil!”
Rafumi, disguised as Ren, had been called to the audience—and Trash had apparently said all this—but Rafumi had seen through the impostor Trash in an instant.
“As for the damage report: an explosion of some kind occurred in both the King’s chambers and Second Princess Melty-sama’s chambers, and within the rooms…”
“Fortunately, I myself escaped unharmed, but…”
“A thorough search of the rooms turned up no bodies belonging to the perpetrators, but the soldiers standing guard suffered tremendous casualties!”
The fake Trash apparently threw both hands up dramatically, striking a prayer-like pose. Truly foolish, I say.
“Oh, Melty…”
“It appears the perpetrators were the Hakuko that the Shield Devil entrusted to you!”

“To think they’d pull such a stunt while I was away… The Shield truly was a devil after all! Reconciliation is out of the question! I hereby rescind the withdrawal of his bounty and return it to null and void—destroy him by any means necessary, and avenge my beloved daughter, Melty!”
From the situation, Rafumi seemed to instantly grasp what thoughts and actions the folks of Melromarc had settled on.
“Is there no way to trace the route—the trail—the perpetrator, the mastermind, used to slip past my watch and vanish from within this castle, this ‘banishment’?”

“We haven’t the faintest idea! But there’s a strong possibility they possess some means of instant transport, much like the one you hold, Sir Amaki. Still, at the very least, they shouldn’t have left the country yet! Sir Amaki, Sword Hero! I have great expectations for your efforts, as the true Hero our Melromarc reveres!”
“I see. Even so, allow me to have the scene investigated as well.”
Rafumi proposed this and moved to search the castle thoroughly, but the fake Trash thrust a hand forward, ordering the soldiers to block him.

“No! I would prefer Sir Amaki prioritize finding them. For that purpose, please, take some of my most trusted men along as companions. Above all, it seems some among them are capable of disguising themselves as doubles resembling myself and Melty. We should assume they intend to further sow chaos within the nation by impersonating us.”
Ha! Aren’t you the ones sowing the chaos here? Taking advantage of the confusion to try and assassinate Trash and my Fiancée, no less.
“The moment you find them, kill anyone who resembles myself or Melty!”
“Understood, Amaki-sama.”

Seizing the perfect opportunity, the fake Trash had apparently forced several of his own loyal men into Ren’s party. Quite the maneuver, I say. What’s more, since the real Trash had supposedly fled, an assassination order was issued declaring that the real one should be killed on sight as an impostor the moment he was found. According to Rafumi, holding back laughter through all of this had been an absolute struggle. And so, King Azott issued the order to track down the vanished Trash, the tiger siblings, and my Fiancée and Filo-tan as well.
